subject.title: Feature request: Auto-send intent/acknowledgment text message before agent processing

question: Should OpenClaw solve pre-processing acknowledgement text as shared messages.ackText config, a non-terminal send-and-continue plugin/channel hook, or only channel-specific placeholder features?
rationale: The requested behavior spans channel UX, config surface, and plugin hook semantics, and the repository policy makes those compatibility-sensitive product boundaries rather than a narrow bug repair.

options.title: Default-off shared ackText config
options.body: Add a canonical messages-level acknowledgement text contract and require each supported channel to opt into the delivery semantics it can implement safely.

options.title: Non-terminal plugin/channel hook
options.body: Expose a typed send-and-continue hook so plugins can implement the UX without adding another global config key.

options.title: Only channel-specific placeholders
options.body: Keep this issue as a tracking parent and let Slack, Telegram, Discord, and other channel-specific placeholder issues define their own behavior independently.

recommendation.title: Default-off shared ackText config
recommendation.body: Add a canonical messages-level acknowledgement text contract and require each supported channel to opt into the delivery semantics it can implement safely.

likelyOwner.reason: The current and recent history ties steipete most directly to the shared config, reply dispatch, and typing lifecycle surfaces that would need to coordinate this decision.
